$comment: Specs KNOWN to fail an attempt and pass on retry. The point is not to
excuse them — it is to make a NEW flake distinguishable from a long-known
one, because on a green shard the two are byte-identical in the log.
ci.yml's 'Name the failing specs' step annotates a known entry as a
::notice (unchanged) and an UNLEDGERED flake as a ::warning. That split is
deliberate and narrow: the step's own comment records that annotating every
green-run flake as an error was measured on run 35427726541 and reverted,
because a step that cries wolf on every green run is one people learn to
ignore. A warning only on something genuinely new is the opposite of that.
Matching is on SPEC FILE + TITLE SUBSTRING, never a line number: a comment
added above a test moves its line (measured — entity-detail-layout went
from :24 to :51 inside one PR) while the test is unchanged.
Deleting an entry is correct the moment a spec is fixed or removed. The
guard asserts every entry's spec file still exists, so a deleted spec
cannot leave its excuse behind. It cannot assert the flake has stopped —
absence is not observable from one run — so that review is a human one.

flakes.title: asset detail page renders the shell
flakes.reason: The App Router transition is DROPPED, not slow: 424 requests with the last at 2.94s then zero network for 29.4s, screencast pixel-static from 2.65s, and the frame URL is /assets/{id} at the start of the expect and /t/{slug}/assets at the end. Cause unidentified — a timeout raise would not help, and the service-worker storm hypothesis measured INCONCLUSIVE (both arms clean) because the flake did not fire in that CI window.

flakes.title: Tasks row double-click navigates to detail
flakes.reason: Same dropped-transition shape as the entity-detail case and in the same E2E shard, which is what made it usable as that experiment's in-run control. Shares expectRouteTransition with it, but the helper is where the failure is CAUGHT rather than caused — ciso-portfolio shows the shape without using it.

flakes.title: CISO creates a 2nd tenant
flakes.reason: The same ~18s shape at its own toBeVisible, and NOT a call site of expectRouteTransition — which is the observation that refuted the shared-helper explanation for this family.
